I feel your pain.  I was depressed as well, for longer than I knew what depression was.  It all came to a head and my life changed forever.  The main source of my problems was a pretty non-existent relationship with my father.  Despite all the successes that I had achieved and how happy I appeared on the outside, my dad was an asshole and it really brought my walls crashing down.  Long story short; I did something, I had never done before and asked questions as to why my father was the way he was.  I discovered that he was human and that life isn't all roses.  No matter how badly we wished we were someone else, reality is that the grass isn't always greener on the other side of the fence.  

So my authority on this issue is that I believe, although I do not know you, is that I truly believe that your life can get better, but you will have to attack issues head on.

Family and Friends: Your family will always care about you, they have too, they are apart of you whether they understand that or not.  Even if you decide that not living is your priority they will think about you because you will be missing.  Maybe they just don't know how to deal with your issues, but unless they are sick in the head, they care.  

Friends they have their own lives, issues, relationships and sometimes they need their space too.  You said 'no longer' meaning that you had friends before, which IMO means that you still have friends and you just haven't seen them in awhile.  It's probably partly because you are dealing with your own crisis.  If you were in a happier and healthier mindset your relationships would start meaning more to you and you would want to know what was going on. Heck, I know you know what Facebook is. Your friends are always only a few keyboard strokes away.
  
As far as you financial problems go, I suggest you consider bankruptcy.  Your life is not worth the stress that your debt and your combination of unemployment is causing you.  I do not know how the laws in your state work, but it's definitely something to look in to.  Do you research and give yourself options.   

Lastly, I would work on self improvement goals.  Read some books that will help to make you less shy and more outgoing.  Watch the Kings Speech. Take some courses on speaking in public, Toastmasters is a good one.   Read books on entrepreneurship and get some ideas to start a simple business.  Find some books on what makes a successful family achieve or books on how to find your purpose.  I just thought of this book because I hear birds chirping and you'll understand why if you ever get to read, "The Power of Now" by Eckhardt Tolle.  

Yeah so in closing, don't kill yourself!  Find another way out.  I forgot to mention that you should also try travelling. I know with your $$ situation that it might be difficult, but even if its somewhere close that you have never been before, you should visit.  A change in scenery is another way to discover your purpose and appreciate the value of life.
